identity.real_world_identity_notes: This is the road-going Valkyrie, distinct from the separately curated Valkyrie Hypercar. Aston Martin specifies a seven-speed sequential shift-by-wire transmission with e-synchronization and pull-away assist.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim with an integrated display and wheel-mounted shift lights.

notes: The modeled pull-away system moved the car from rest without physical clutch input.
All seven paddle-selected gears accepted clutchless shifts and automatic downshift blip was directly observed.
Automatic cut was manually confirmed from the throttle graph and is retained at medium confidence.
Guided test completed in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch and Auto Shifting disabled and no separate throttle-blip assist available.
Automatic cut was manually confirmed by the observer after the guided detector returned an uncertain trace.

confidence.basis: Manufacturer specifications and exact guided testing agree on the seven-speed paddle interface and automated pull-away; automatic cut is separately retained at medium confidence.

claims.basis: Official release context and exact live telemetry establish the road-car identity and class.
Aston Martin's specification and exact live behavior agree on seven-speed shift-by-wire operation with pull-away assist.
Guided current-game testing directly established automatic downshift blip and cockpit wheel details.
The observer manually confirmed a throttle cut after the automated trace was inconclusive.

notes: The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
